label: chairperson of
definition: The first person is or was chairperson of the second organization.
scope_notes: Chairman noun and possessive paths and chairmanship succession dominate. Historical, resigning or retiring chairpersons are included. The smaller executive/founder family is competing evidence: an executive need not chair the organization. Do not widen this clear office to every managerial role.

facts.reason: Reed is explicitly chairman of Citicorp in three direct constructions; the executive and long attachment rows are not needed for support.
All supplied Greenspan/Fed rows explicitly state chairmanship.
Lay is directly Enron chairman. Executive and founder rows express additional roles, while the direct chairman paths establish this fact.
Both rows identify Lamoriello as a Devils executive, which does not establish that he is their chairperson.
The ordered pair is State Department to Rubin and the path concerns the department's spokesman saying something; it is neither person-to-organization chairmanship nor the correct role.
